handoff.purpose: Defines _git_run() with hardening logic and subprocess call, and TaskSpec/RunnerContext dataclasses for attempt metadata.

symbols.name: _git_run
symbols.note: Runs git subprocess with optional hardening. Contains the only subprocess call in the module per comments.

symbols.name: TaskSpec
symbols.note: Immutable dataclass representing what is being attempted. Contains fields for task_id, instruction, base_revision, gate_paths, metadata, target_paths, gate_argv, gate_cwd, gate_timeout_s, fail_to_pass, pass_to_pass, correctness_before_state.

symbols.name: TaskSpec.body
symbols.note: Returns canonical JSON-safe dict for digestion. Conditionally includes target_paths, gate, and correctness keys.

symbols.name: TaskSpec.digest
symbols.note: Returns SHA-256 hex digest of canonical JSON of body().

symbols.name: RunnerContext
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass for runner/gate context. No repo_root field by design.

claims.text: THE ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION, and it is narrowed so it cannot be reused. `_inherited_config_args` has to read the operator's REAL config -- that is the whole question it asks -- and the hardened environment exists to hide exactly that. So the exception is allowed only for a `config` read, which cannot write and cannot execute anything. Any other verb asking for it is a bug in this module, so it raises rather than degrading.
claims.why: The code checks 'if not harden and verb != "config": raise ValueError(...)' but the function signature does not show 'verb' as a parameter; it is presumably passed via *args. The claim about _inherited_config_args and hardened environment is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: ONE subprocess call in this module, and a test asserts there is exactly one -- a second would be a way around the primary-checkout guard above. `harden` therefore changes the ARGUMENTS to this call, never whether the call goes through here.
claims.why: The chunk shows exactly one subprocess.run call. The claim about a test asserting exactly one call and about the primary-checkout guard cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Empty values preserve the original/manual harness: no declared target scope means the attempt is unconstrained, and no command argv means the existing pytest gate derived from ``gate_paths`` is used.
claims.why: The docstring describes behavior that depends on how empty fields are handled elsewhere (e.g., in TaskAttempt.__init__). The code in this chunk only defines the dataclass with defaults; the claimed fallback logic is not present.

claims.text: SWE-bench's FAIL_TO_PASS / PASS_TO_PASS schema (docs/ABSORPTION.md F1), a per-task discrimination criterion instead of "the whole suite is green": node ids that must go from failing to passing, and node ids that must stay passing. Empty (the default) means no correctness task is declared and the gate falls through to gate_argv/gate_paths exactly as before -- see the precedence note on TaskAttempt.__init__.
claims.why: The claim references external documentation (docs/ABSORPTION.md) and another class (TaskAttempt.__init__). The code only defines the fields; the behavior described is not implemented here.

claims.text: ``correctness_before_state`` is the FROZEN, PRE-VERIFIED receipt these lists were measured under (the shape ``daedalus.eval.correctness.seed_task_from_commit``/the correctness corpus already produces: ``verified``, ``base_revision``, ``selection_digest``, per-node status maps). It is carried here, not re-derived, because the candidate's worktree already has the patch applied by the time a gate runs -- the before-state CANNOT be measured there, only checked against a receipt made earlier. Present but unverified/mismatched is refused at gate time by ``daedalus.eval.correctness.correctness_gate`` itself, never treated as passing; that fail-closed behaviour is the existing, tested one, not reimplemented here.
claims.why: The claim describes behavior in another module (daedalus.eval.correctness.correctness_gate) and references external functions. The code in this chunk only stores the field; the verification logic is not present.

claims.text: Preserve every legacy TaskSpec digest/effect key byte-for-byte. Curated fields join the canonical body only when that task actually declares them.
claims.why: The claim about byte-for-byte preservation cannot be verified without knowing the legacy digest format. The code conditionally adds fields, which is consistent with the claim, but the claim's specificity is uncheckable.

claims.text: There is no ``repo_root`` field, and that absence is load-bearing: a runner that cannot name the primary checkout cannot write it by accident.
claims.why: The dataclass definition does not include a repo_root field. The claim is consistent with the code shown.

observations.what: The function _git_run() is defined but its signature is not shown in this chunk; it is called with arguments that include *args and keywords like cwd_path, timeout, check, harden, git_dir, work_tree, verb. The verb parameter is used in a condition but not declared in the visible code.

The comment about 'ONE DELIBERATE EXCEPTION' for config reads is partially implemented: the code raises ValueError if not harden and verb != 'config'. However, it does not validate that verb is actually 'config' for the allowed case; it only checks inequality.

The subprocess.run call uses 'capture_output=True' and a timeout, but does not handle subprocess.TimeoutExpired exception. The code only checks returncode; a timeout would raise an exception not caught here.

TaskSpec.body() method returns a dict that may contain keys like 'gate' and 'correctness' conditionally. The 'before_state' key under 'correctness' uses _jsonable(dict(self.correctness_before_state)). If correctness_before_state contains non-serializable values, _jsonable may fail.
TaskSpec.digest property uses canonical_json(self.body()) which is not defined in this chunk. It is assumed to be imported or defined elsewhere.
